title: Grateful Dead Live at Seminole Indian Village on 1969-05-23

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of a 1969 gem with an epic Dark Star and soaring Morning Dew, delivered in crystal‑clear mix.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine soundboard tape that lets every instrument shine – from Jerry’s sweet guitar tone and vocal presence to Phil’s thumping bass and the dual‑drummer cymbal fireworks. Musically the show shines on Dark Star’s two‑jam adventure, a soaring Morning Dew, plus standout renditions of St. Stephen and The Eleven, making it one of the era’s most coveted performances.

ai_rating.rationale: All seven reviews are overwhelmingly positive (5‑star range) and consistently praise both the exceptional soundboard quality and the high‑level musical performance, with only minor setlist complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the tape as amazingly clear, every instrument audible, low end solid, vocals present and juicy; noted as better than other known sources and free of noticeable drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: High energy throughout with a powerful first jam of Dark Star, an explosive second jam highlighted by crashing cymbals, and a seamless transition into the soaring Morning Dew; set feels cohesive despite the omission of Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is described as perfect and his vocals are fine and present – a rare early‑'69 vocal strength.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is praised for its thumping power on Morning Dew and the pounding bass sequence in The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both drummers receive kudos for amazing whooshing cymbal crashes that punctuate Dark Star’s second jam.
